summary.text: Analise Sherlock is Labor's candidate for Evelyn, a Liberal-held seat, at the 2026 Victorian election. She lives in Lilydale and has worked for the nurses' union, assisting members with workplace rights, and on a public transport project, dealing with residents affected by the construction. Labor's page says her first job was in retail.

sources.title: Evelyn: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

priorities.text: honest leadership based on evidence, listening to locals
Better access to childcare, healthcare, schools and dependable public transport in Evelyn
Properly funding the CFA and SES as climate change adds to the demands on them
Reducing the influence of big money on politics

summary.text: Andrew Henley is again the Greens candidate for Evelyn, having taken 9.3% of first preferences there in 2022. A healthcare worker and father, he has lived in Mooroolbark for 14 years. He argues that local services have not kept pace with the area's growth and that integrity in government underpins better services.

sources.title: Evelyn: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Andrew Henley, Candidate for Evelyn, Australian Greens
Candidates of the 2022 Victorian state election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Bridget Vallence has been the Liberal member for Evelyn since 2018. She has held a run of shadow portfolios and is now shadow minister for finance, jobs and skills, and trade and investment, having been Manager of Opposition Business for most of 2025. Before Parliament she spent 16 years in automotive procurement, and she is recontesting Evelyn in 2026.

occupation.text: Procurement professional in the automotive industry

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for Jobs and Skills
Shadow Minister for WorkSafe and TAC
Shadow Minister for Trade and Investment

summary.text: Daniel Killey is One Nation's candidate for Evelyn at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC says he is a psychologist who set up a community mental health practice, after 15 years in the Australian Defence Force as a combat engineer. Born in South Africa, he grew up in Melbourne's outer east. One Nation's candidate page refused automated access, so it could not be checked.

sources.title: Evelyn: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

priorities.text: Let me fight for you, and for a society that puts people before profit.
Relief from rising house prices, rents and childcare costs that have outstripped wages
Politics that does not target the most vulnerable people

summary.text: James Scanlon is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Evelyn at the 2026 Victorian election. An Army veteran from Mooroolbark, he spent close to ten years as an officer, and the ABC says he studied mechanical engineering at RMIT to associate degree level. His campaign focuses on housing, rent and childcare costs running ahead of wages.

sources.title: Evelyn: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Jan Heald is standing for the Animal Justice Party in Evelyn at the 2026 Victorian election, as she did in 2022. Her working life has been in customer service and public relations, and for 14 years she held the secretary's post at the Australian Wildlife Protection Council. She has also led a local volunteer group, Friends of the Mt Evelyn Aqueduct Trail, as president, and the party says she joined it when it was formed in 2009.

summary.text: Michelle O'Brien is the Family First candidate for Evelyn at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Writing on her party page, she says she lives in the electorate, is the mother of four school-age children and has a long background working in disability support and aged care. She lists traffic, road and infrastructure pressure, community safety, housing affordability and the cost of living as the main local issues.

occupation.text: Aged care and disability support worker

priorities.text: If elected, I will be a strong local voice for Evelyn
Easing traffic congestion and the strain on local roads and infrastructure
Relief from high rents, taxes, fuel and power bills
Backing local businesses instead of burdening them
Advocacy for children, older Victorians and people with disability
